minutes_text:
Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES ‐ April 7, 2022

A meeting of the Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission was convened on April 7, 2022, via
Zoom. Commissioner Denmon called the meeting to order at 6:07 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Roll Call

Present
  Commissioner Lee Denmon, District One
  Commissioner Jacob Fragoso, District Two
  Commissioner Cynthia, McLemore, District Three
  Sabrina Barnes, Director-Parks, Recreation, and Community Services
  Thomas Uwal, Human Services Superintendent
  Gilbert Gonzalez, Graffiti Abatement Supervisor
  Anthony Harris, Recreation Supervisor
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
Absent
  Commissioner Christopher Beck, District Four
  Commissioner Henry Brown, Commissioner at Large

Public Comments

  None

Approval of the Minutes

  Commissioner Fragoso made the motion to approve the minutes from March 3, 2022.
Commissioner McLemore seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Fragoso, McLemore, and Denmon
  Nays: None

Staff Report

  Stephanie Maldonado presented a staff report recommending the Park and Recreation
Commission recommend the Mayor and Council Members reject all bids received on March 9, 2022
for the Darby Park Restroom Project, CB-22-03 and authorize the rebid of the project.

  Commissioner Fragoso made a motion to approve the staff report. Commissioner Denmon
seconded and the motion was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Fragoso, McLemore, and Denmon
  Nays: None

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES ‐ April 7, 2022
Verbal Reports

  Gilbert Gonzalez gave a verbal report on behalf of the Parks Administration regarding the
following:
   50 flats of gazanias and 50 flats of purple ice plants were planted along the center median
  on Manchester Boulevard from Prairie Avenue to Crenshaw Drive.
   Six (6) camphor trees that were vandalized at Edward Vincent Jr Park were replanted.
   The Graffiti Abatement staff has been busy in all districts especially Districts 1, 2 and 4.
   Staff repainted the baseball bleachers at both Rogers and Edward Vincent Jr Parks. Darby
  Park will be completed soon.

  Anthony Harris gave a verbal report on behalf of the Recreation Division regarding the
following:
   On Saturday, April 9, 2022, the Parks, Recreation and Community Service Department in
  partnership with Science of Sport will host the first annual Inglewood STEM Fest from 9:00
  a.m. to 1:00 p.m. at Edward Vincent Jr, Park. The free event will expose students in grades
  kindergarten through sixth to science, technology, engineering and math (STEM) through
  experiences that focus on several familiar sports. This inaugural event is designed to bring
  Los Angeles-based sports organizations to provide an engaging day of STEM and sports to
  the Inglewood community. Activity stations will be set-up throughout the event providing
  STEM lessons centered on breath work & yoga, basketball, soccer, tennis, baseball, softball,
  football and track & field. The event will also feature STEM presentation by Science of Sport
  and a panel discussion with industry professionals. Community partners for the inaugural
  event include Angel City Football Club, Los Angeles Dodgers Foundation, Los Angeles
  Lakers, Los Angeles Rams, The Marvin Group, USTA So Cal, LAFC (Los Angeles Football
  Cub), Los Angeles Clippers, Los Angeles Chargers, LA Galaxy, Morgan Stanley, First
  Republic Bank and LINXS Constructors. We encourage you to stop by if your schedule
  permits
   This year Earth Day will be held on Friday, April 22, 2022. We are excited to partner with
  Hollywood Park to host a beautification project at Darby Park from 9:00 a.m. to noon. The
  event will include planting of new tress, sprucing up existing planters and adding some curb
  appeal to the parking lot with the planting of additional plants and flowers. On Saturday, April
  23, 2022. Our own a local non-profit organization will partner with the Dobby Garden to
  beautify the garden area at Rogers Park. Volunteers from the organizations will clean up
  and re-plant existing planters, add new garden beds, and clean up the patio area. The group
  organizers will maintain the area and host workshops throughout the year.
   We are excited to announce a Palm Painting class for tots ages 3-5. The Department has
  partnered with Budding Artist - a non-profit organization committed to providing young
  children with art experiences. The FREE one-hour class will be held on Saturday, May 7,
  2022 at Siminiski Park. Registration is open to Inglewood residents. Register at
  www.parksrec@cityofinglewood.org
   After 9 weeks of screening, vetting weekly COVID tests and limited attendance at games,
  tonight represents Championship Thursday for our All American and Prep divisions of the

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES ‐ April 7, 2022
  Inglewood Youth Basketball League. Saturday will be the final day of competition for the Pee
  Wee, Tom Thumb and Junior divisions. We are proud and fortunate our Junior teams were
  able to partner with our neighbors in Hawthorne to create a full league with 6 teams. I am
  proud to report that both our Rogers Park and Darby Park teams made the playoffs. The two
  Inglewood teams clashed in the semi-finals with Darby Park coming away with the victory.
  Our Darby Park team will play on Saturday, April 9, 2022 for the league Championship at
  the Betty Ainsworth Sports Center with the game beginning at 1:30 p.m. The season will
  conclude this weekend as all teams celebrate the season with food, fun and awards at
  Shakey’s Pizza in Inglewood.
    Are you ready for some baseball? The Dodgers Dreamteam (formerly Dodgers RBI) spring
  season in Inglewood begins next week for 175 players. The spring season is designed
  specifically to focus on the younger age groups (ages 5-6 T-ball, 7-8 Coach Pitch). The 5-
  week season is a developmental environment that will introduce the game while honing in
  on the fundamentals of throwing, catching, hitting and base running. There are a total of 14
  teams with seven (7) in each division. Teams will practice out of both Darby and Edward
  Vincent Parks. The season will consist of nine (9) games in 5-weeks playing under the lights
  on Wednesday evenings and all day on Saturday’s. The opening ceremony is scheduled for
  Saturday, April 16, 2022 from 9:00 a.m. – 11:00 a.m. We look forward to the fun. Some of
  you may be wondering when the older age groups begin. Registration for the Minors, Majors,
  Junior Softball, Junior Baseball, Sr. Baseball and Sr. Softball begins April 18, 2022 with the
  season set to begin in mid-June.

  Thomas Uwal gave a verbal report on behalf of the Human Services Division regarding the
following:
   The Inglewood Senior Center recently re-opened its doors to provide seniors with classes
  and activities. More recently with the city slowly opening up starting in April 2022, the Senior
  Center has begun to allow more seniors to schedule classes. Seniors are still expected to
  wear full-face coverings, have their temperatures checked and provide proof of full
  vaccination. These measures are required in order to enter and participate in
  activities. These measures will remain until further notice to continue to ensure our seniors
  are as safe as possible.
   Our Senior and Disabled Transportation Program continues to provide trips to critical
  appointments such as dialysis and doctors’ appointments. Drivers as well as passengers
  continue to wear mandated face masks coverings. We have also been scheduling our drivers
  to transport our seniors and persons with disabilities to other next day requested
  appointments. Our free trolley service which has 24 stops on its fixed route is now back in
  operation in the city of Inglewood. It operates from 10:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. Monday through
  Friday and is free to the public to ride.
   The Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) continues to provide Grab-N-Go meals
  to youth 18 and younger at three (3) sites (Crenshaw Library, Rogers Park and Darby Park).
  We continue to serve meals to our youth and the number of meals are expected to increase
  as COVID restrictions are easing. We are also in the process of issuing an RFP to renew
  our contract in September 2022.

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES ‐ April 7, 2022
    Our Nutrition program provides seven meals per week to approximately 300 senior residents
  of Inglewood. We continue to provide monthly shelf stable meal packages in collaboration
  with the Los Angeles Food Bank, and weekly fresh produce deliveries in collaboration with
  the Social Justice Learning Institute. We have sourced 600 COVID-19 testing kits from Los
  Angeles Workforce Development, Aging and Community Services (WDACS) which will be
  distributed to seniors.

Director’s Report

  Sabrina Barnes gave a verbal update regarding the following Capital Improvement Projects
currently in progress:
   Vincent Park Restroom Construction
   Groundbreaking of the Vincent Park Pump Track
   Unveiling of the renovated outdoor basketball courts at Rogers Park
   Walking track at Darby Park
   Playground resurfacing at Vincent, Rogers, Darby and Siminski Parks

  Commissioner McLemore asked if the restrooms are complete at Vincent Park. Sabrina
Barnes stated no, one (1) has been completed and we are currently working on the second. Once
completed we will go to Darby Park to renovate, then return to Vincent Park with Queen Park to
follow.

Public Comments

  Imhotep Coleman stated the courts at Rogers Park are beautiful and asked if staff has ever
considered constructing a pathway to courts. He also thanked everyone for their services. Sabrina
Barnes stated yes, we are considering it as part of an upcoming parking lot resurfacing project.

Commissioner’s Comments

  Commissioner Denmon stated he recently took a walk around the lake at SoFi Stadium and
asked if it is open to public. Sabrina Barnes stated to my understanding it is open and you can drive
in and park when open.

With no further business, the meeting was adjourned at 6:35 p.m.
